title: 40q tensornet-mps single-point evaluation — the one owed deliverable, pre-registered
purpose: Close the single remaining gap flagged by the HPC/CUDA-Q reviewer: prove CUDA-Q's tensornet-mps backend actually samples QSCI determinants at the full 40-qubit scale on one GPU. This is the SAMPLER-at-scale proof, NOT a full growth-to-chemical-accuracy run (that is the expensive multi-day version, scoped separately below and deliberately not pre-committed).
system: H20 chain, 40 qubits, STO-6G, Jordan-Wigner — identical Hamiltonian to E3/E6 (same committed integrals).
what_runs: Load the committed 40q Hamiltonian; prepare an MP2-seeded UCC state; sample the dominant determinant subspace via CUDA-Q tensornet-mps (bond dimension chi=400, the measured chemical-accuracy target from mps_bonddim_study.py) on one 80GB GPU; diagonalize H in that subspace (QSCI); compare to the committed block2 DMRG(chi=400) reference that predates access.

predictions.P8a_backend_runs_at_40q: tensornet-mps sampling completes at 40 qubits without exceeding 80 GB device memory (the whole point of MPS vs the ~16 TB exact statevector).
predictions.P8b_energy_consistency: the tensornet-mps-sampled QSCI energy at a matched determinant budget lands within +/-1.6 mHa of the incremental-engine value the flagship already committed at the same budget (seed/sampler-path independence, already validated at 20q/28q where the device sampler was exact).
predictions.P8c_memory: peak device memory < 8 GB at chi=400 (consistent with the crossover_study.py projection of ~0.2 GB MPS footprint).

reference: results/gpu_run1_h20_mp2seed_evidence.json (committed flagship, +1.226 mHa vs DMRG chi=400 at 450,257 dets) and the committed block2 DMRG(chi=400) energy -10.29219417780498 Ha.

resource_ceiling.abort_gate: hard stop at 6 h GPU wall-clock regardless of state; report as-measured (pass, partial, or DNF) exactly like E2/E3/E5.
resource_ceiling.instance: one NVIDIA A100/H100 (80 GB) on qBraid; CUDAQ_TARGET=tensornet-mps

cost_estimate_committed_ratecard.basis: qBraid GPU on-demand ~= 6.40 cr/min class instance (published rate card in src/cost_audit.py); credit-to-USD from the committed OpenQuantum conversion ~$0.010/cr.
cost_estimate_committed_ratecard.single_point_eval: <= 6 h ceiling => <= ~2,300 cr => ~$23 worst-case; a clean run is expected in ~1-3 h (~600-1,150 cr, ~$6-12).
cost_estimate_committed_ratecard.full_growth_to_chem_acc_NOT_committed: a full 40q tensornet-mps growth-to-chemical-accuracy run is the multi-day version the flagship deliberately pivoted away from (MPS-contraction cost at 40q); realistic 2-7 GPU-days => ~28k-97k cr => ~$280-970, with real risk of not converging inside budget. Not pre-committed here; flagged so the spend is a conscious choice.

honesty_clause: Outcome reported exactly as measured — pass, partial, or DNF — with the same discipline as E2-E6. A DNF (e.g. MPS contraction too slow at 40q) is itself the honest, publishable finding that motivated the MP2-seed engine, and does not retroactively weaken any committed result.
note: Pre-registration only. Freezing this protocol is not a commitment to run it; it exists so that IF run on qBraid, thresholds and reference are fixed in git beforehand, exactly like preregistration_v2 / _e67.
